name: getcwd
description: The getcwd function retrieves the absolute pathname of the current working directory and copies it to a provided buffer. If the buffer is NULL, it allocates one dynamically using malloc. Other variants like get_current_dir_name and getwd provide similar functionality but with different memory handling and are either GNU-specific or deprecated.

parameters.name: buf
parameters.description: Buffer to hold the absolute pathname of the current working directory

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Size of the buffer; if less than required, returns NULL and sets errno to ERANGE

return_value.success: Returns a pointer to a string containing the pathname of the current working directory
return_value.failure: Returns NULL, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: Permission to read or search a component of the filename was denied
buf points to a bad address
The size argument is zero and buf is not a null pointer, or for getwd, buf is NULL
For getwd, the size of the pathname exceeds PATH_MAX bytes
The current working directory has been unlinked
The size argument is less than the length of the pathname, including the null byte

bugs: Since Linux 2.6.36, glibc's getcwd() failed to return an absolute pathname in certain cases, violating POSIX; this was corrected in glibc 2.27, where it now fails with ENOENT instead.
versions: POSIX.1-2001; Linux kernel since 2.1.92, with changes up to Linux 3.12 and beyond
